name: Arginine (AAKG)
summary: Arginine alpha-ketoglutarate, a pre-workout 'pump' supplement whose small human trials mostly report no performance benefit.
lead: Arginine alpha-ketoglutarate (AAKG) is a dietary supplement made of the amino acid L-arginine paired with alpha-ketoglutaric acid, typically in a 2:1 molar ratio, and marketed as more soluble or bioavailable than arginine alone. It is sold mainly to athletes and bodybuilders as a pre-workout ingredient intended to raise nitric oxide, improve muscle blood flow and increase strength or endurance.

name: BCAA
summary: Leucine, isoleucine and valine powders sold for muscle and recovery; the mechanism is real but supplement-specific human evidence is limited.
lead: Branched-chain amino acids (BCAAs) are the three essential amino acids with a branched side chain: leucine, isoleucine and valine. Humans cannot synthesise them and obtain them from dietary protein . They are sold as stand-alone powders and capsules, mainly to people who lift weights, with claims about muscle growth, recovery and reduced soreness.

name: ZMA
summary: A zinc, magnesium and B6 night-time supplement sold for sleep and testosterone; the few studies conflict.
lead: ZMA is a supplement combining zinc, magnesium and vitamin B6, marketed to athletes, gymnasts and bodybuilders. It was developed by Victor Conte, the founder of BALCO Laboratories . The standard formulation contains zinc monomethionine aspartate, magnesium aspartate and pyridoxine hydrochloride (vitamin B6) .

name: Beef organ / beef juice extract
summary: Concentrated beef organ or meat-juice products marketed as nutrient-dense muscle support; product-specific human evidence is thin.
lead: Beef organ and beef juice or meat extract supplements are concentrated products derived from cattle meat or offal, sold as nutrient-dense foods or capsules for muscle and general health. Offal means the internal organs of a butchered animal, and these are eaten in many cuisines . Meat extract is a concentrated stock, first developed commercially in the nineteenth century .

name: Dimethylglycine (DMG)
summary: A glycine derivative once called vitamin B16, sold for endurance and immunity; trials in other conditions have shown little benefit.
lead: Dimethylglycine (DMG) is a derivative of the amino acid glycine with two methyl groups on the nitrogen. It forms during the breakdown of betaine (trimethylglycine) and choline, and occurs in foods such as beans and liver . It was once called vitamin B16, though it is not considered a true vitamin because deficiency causes no ill effects .

name: Magnesium glycinate
summary: A glycine-bound magnesium supplement popular for sleep and calm; the claims outrun the glycinate-specific trials.
lead: Magnesium glycinate, also called magnesium bisglycinate or diglycinate, is the magnesium salt of glycine, containing about 14.1 percent elemental magnesium by mass . It is sold as a supplement to relieve magnesium deficiency and also appears in cosmetics . Marketing often presents it as better tolerated and more absorbable than magnesium oxide, and it is popular for sleep, relaxation and recovery .
claims: Magnesium glycinate stacked with L-theanine and GABA improves or lengthens sleep

name: Magnesium malate
summary: Magnesium bound to malic acid, pitched for energy, soreness and fibromyalgia; direct human evidence is thin.
lead: Magnesium malate is the magnesium salt of malic acid, sold as a mineral supplement . Wikipedia notes it is discussed as more bioavailable than citrate or glycinate, citing a single supplier source . Supplement sellers also promote it for muscle soreness, exercise recovery and fibromyalgia pain .

name: Inositol nicotinate
summary: A no-flush niacin ester sold as a supplement; studied for circulation, with nothing published on appearance.
lead: Inositol nicotinate, also called inositol hexanicotinate or inositol hexaniacinate, is a compound formed from niacin (vitamin B3) and inositol. In the United States it is sold as a dietary supplement, marketed as a "no-flush" form of niacin, and the body is described as breaking it down into its two components .

name: Pyridoxamine
summary: A vitamin B6 form studied as an AGE inhibitor in diabetic kidney disease, with no appearance research.
lead: Pyridoxamine is one of the three natural forms of vitamin B6. Its chemistry allows it to scavenge free radicals and reactive carbonyl compounds and to chelate metal ions . It is discussed in longevity and skin circles as an inhibitor of advanced glycation end products (AGEs), compounds linked in the literature to diabetic complications and tissue ageing .

name: D-Ribose-L-cysteine
summary: A patented cysteine prodrug marketed to raise glutathione; research is preclinical and nothing covers appearance.
lead: D-Ribose-L-cysteine (DRLC), sold under the names RiboCeine and RibCys, is a patented synthetic compound intended to deliver L-cysteine to cells and so support the body's own glutathione production . Glutathione is a cellular antioxidant, and cysteine availability is described as the limiting factor in making it .

name: Eutropoflavin (7,8-DHF)
summary: A plant flavone reported to activate the BDNF receptor TrkB in animals; no human studies exist.
lead: 7,8-Dihydroxyflavone (7,8-DHF), also called tropoflavin, is a naturally occurring flavone found in plants such as Godmania aesculifolia, Tridax procumbens and Primula vulgaris. It was reported in a 2010 PNAS paper as a small-molecule agonist of TrkB, the main receptor for brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) .

name: 5-HTP (oxitriptan)
summary: A serotonin precursor sold for mood and sleep; many trials registered, none about looks.
lead: 5-Hydroxytryptophan (5-HTP), medically oxitriptan, is a naturally occurring amino acid and intermediate in serotonin synthesis. The body makes it from tryptophan via tryptophan hydroxylase, the rate-limiting step, and unlike serotonin it crosses the blood-brain barrier . Food contains only insignificant amounts .

name: L-Tryptophan
summary: An essential amino acid sold for sleep and mood; evidence is weak and a 1989 contamination outbreak shaped its regulation.
lead: Tryptophan is an essential amino acid that humans cannot make and must obtain from protein foods such as meat, dairy, eggs, nuts and seeds. Besides building proteins it is a precursor of serotonin, melatonin and niacin . Frederick Hopkins first isolated it in 1901 from casein .

name: Ramelteon
summary: A prescription melatonin-receptor sleep drug with small, medical-only evidence and nothing on appearance.
lead: Ramelteon is a prescription melatonin receptor agonist taken by mouth for insomnia characterised by difficulty falling asleep. It binds the MT1 and MT2 melatonin receptors and, according to its US label, has no appreciable affinity for the GABA receptor complex used by benzodiazepines and Z-drugs . It was approved by the US FDA in 2005 under the brand name Rozerem and is not a controlled substance in the United States .

name: Tasimelteon
summary: A prescription circadian drug approved for non-24-hour disorder in blind people; no appearance evidence.
lead: Tasimelteon is a prescription melatonin MT1/MT2 receptor agonist developed by Vanda Pharmaceuticals and sold as Hetlioz. The US FDA approved it in January 2014 for Non-24-Hour Sleep-Wake Disorder in adults, and in December 2020 for nighttime sleep disturbances in Smith-Magenis syndrome .

name: Agomelatine
summary: A melatonin-linked antidepressant sold in Europe, not the US; no appearance evidence.
lead: Agomelatine is an antidepressant developed by Servier and sold as Valdoxan. It is an agonist at melatonin MT1 and MT2 receptors and an antagonist at serotonin 5-HT2C receptors . It was authorised in the European Union in 2009 and is available in several other countries, but it has not been approved by the US FDA .

name: Hydroxyzine
summary: A sedating prescription antihistamine for anxiety and itch; nothing on appearance.
lead: Hydroxyzine is a first-generation antihistamine of the piperazine class, approved by the US FDA in 1956. Its US label covers symptomatic relief of anxiety and tension, itching from allergic conditions such as chronic urticaria and atopic or contact dermatitis, and sedation before and after general anaesthesia .

name: Low-dose doxepin (Silenor)
summary: A prescription low-dose tricyclic approved for sleep-maintenance insomnia; no appearance evidence.
lead: Doxepin is a tricyclic compound first approved by the US FDA in 1969 as an antidepressant under the brand name Sinequan. A low-dose oral tablet, Silenor, was approved in 2010 for insomnia characterised by difficulty staying asleep . A 5% topical cream is approved for itching in atopic dermatitis or lichen simplex chronicus .

name: Suvorexant
summary: A prescription orexin-blocking sleep drug; solid insomnia data, no appearance evidence.
lead: Suvorexant is a dual orexin receptor antagonist developed by Merck and sold as Belsomra. The US FDA approved it in August 2014 as the first drug of its class for insomnia characterised by difficulty with sleep onset and/or maintenance . It blocks orexin A and B at OX1 and OX2 receptors, reducing wake-promoting signalling rather than acting through GABA .

name: Lemborexant
summary: A prescription orexin-blocking sleep drug (Dayvigo); studied only for insomnia, with no appearance studies at all.
lead: Lemborexant, sold as Dayvigo, is a prescription oral medicine for adults with insomnia involving trouble falling asleep, staying asleep, or both. It was developed by Eisai and belongs to the dual orexin receptor antagonist (DORA) class, which blocks the wake-promoting orexin (hypocretin) signalling system rather than enhancing GABA activity as benzodiazepines and Z-drugs do.

name: Daridorexant
summary: A prescription orexin-blocking insomnia drug (Quviviq); no appearance research exists.
lead: Daridorexant, sold as Quviviq, is a prescription dual orexin receptor antagonist for adults with insomnia involving difficulty falling asleep or staying asleep. It was developed by Idorsia Pharmaceuticals and was formerly known as nemorexant during development.

name: Eszopiclone
summary: A prescription Z-drug sleeping pill (Lunesta); sleep research only, nothing on appearance.
lead: Eszopiclone, sold as Lunesta and as generics, is a prescription nonbenzodiazepine hypnotic of the cyclopyrrolone class. It is the active (S)-enantiomer of zopiclone and is used for insomnia in adults.

name: Zaleplon
summary: A short-acting prescription Z-drug sleeping pill (Sonata); no appearance data.
lead: Zaleplon, sold as Sonata, is a prescription nonbenzodiazepine hypnotic (pyrazolopyrimidine class) approved for short-term treatment of insomnia, particularly difficulty falling asleep.

name: Zopiclone
summary: A prescription Z-drug sleeping pill (Imovane); not US-approved and untested for looks.
lead: Zopiclone is a prescription nonbenzodiazepine hypnotic of the cyclopyrrolone class used for short-term treatment of severe insomnia in adults. It acts at the benzodiazepine site of the GABA-A receptor.
claims: Sleeping pills like zopiclone improve sleep but harm sleep quality over time.

name: Temazepam
summary: A prescription benzodiazepine sleeping pill; sleep research only, no appearance data.
lead: Temazepam is a short-to-intermediate-acting benzodiazepine hypnotic prescribed for short-term treatment of insomnia. It enhances GABA-A receptor activity, producing sedation, and is a Schedule IV controlled substance in the US.

name: Gabapentin
summary: A prescription nerve-pain and seizure drug that some people take off-label for sleep; proven for neuropathic pain, untested for looks.
lead: Gabapentin is a prescription anticonvulsant and analgesic that is structurally related to the neurotransmitter GABA but, according to its US label, has no effect on GABA binding, uptake or degradation. It is sold under brand names including Neurontin and Gralise . The US label lists management of postherpetic neuralgia and adjunctive treatment of partial-onset seizures as its approved uses .

name: Pregabalin
summary: A prescription nerve-pain and anxiety-adjacent drug that forum users take to lower social inhibition; untested for that use and carries misuse and withdrawal risks.
lead: Pregabalin is a prescription gabapentinoid, structurally related to GABA, sold by Pfizer as Lyrica. The US label lists diabetic peripheral neuropathic pain, postherpetic neuralgia, fibromyalgia, spinal-cord-injury neuropathic pain and adjunctive treatment of partial-onset seizures .
claims: Pregabalin removes social anxiety and lowers inhibition.
Withdrawal from pregabalin can be severe.

name: Mirtazapine
summary: A sedating, appetite-boosting prescription antidepressant sometimes used off-label for sleep; approved for depression, untested for looks.
lead: Mirtazapine is a tetracyclic antidepressant, classed as a noradrenergic and specific serotonergic antidepressant, sold as Remeron. The US label lists major depressive disorder in adults as its indication .

name: Sodium oxybate (GHB)
summary: A narcolepsy prescription drug that is chemically GHB; approved for sleep disorders, untested for looks, and tightly controlled for serious safety reasons.
lead: Sodium oxybate is the sodium salt of gamma-hydroxybutyrate (GHB), a central nervous system depressant. As a prescription product it is approved in the US for cataplexy and excessive daytime sleepiness in narcolepsy . The same compound is also a controlled drug outside medical use.

name: Prazosin
summary: A blood-pressure alpha-blocker used off-label for trauma nightmares; nothing connects it to appearance.
lead: Prazosin is an alpha-1 adrenergic receptor blocker. The US label lists hypertension as its indication . Reference sources describe off-label use for benign prostatic hyperplasia, Raynaud's phenomenon and nightmares associated with post-traumatic stress disorder .
